issues.claim: The damage layer has two rules for a roofless wing's roof bays. §2.6 step 7 (l.2085–2086) calls the threshold test "the one comparison every reader makes": an element is damaged when the level reaches its t, otherwise not. V03 §5.6 (2) (c) (l.2697–2702) and V02 §5.7 (2) (l.3064–3066; X34, T-V2-59 (b)) also mark every roof bay over a room of a roofless wing (`RoofSpec.kind 'none'`: the decline's `decayed` and `ruined` states, a fire's `charred` shell) as damaged, whatever its threshold. That is what keeps the inside and the outside in agreement (item 123 (d)): V06 §3.23 (2) starts a `decayed` building at level 1/3, and V11's `roofBay` range is 0.40–0.66 (l.4596). So a newly roofless building has no roof over it on the exterior, while under §2.6's one comparison every roof bay in its plan stays intact. The rule is shared by two volumes but stated only in them, and the base's home denies it.
issues.required_change: §2.6 step 7, after the comparison sentence: "One case has no threshold: while a building is `decayed` or `ruined` — in a decay run, or read at V11's default age with no run in the log (V06 §3.23 (4)) — every roof bay over a room of a wing whose `RoofSpec.kind` is `none` (the decline's roofless state, a fire's charred shell) is damaged whatever its t, so the plan's open ceilings are the roof the exterior lacks (item 123 (d)); nesting holds, the state only climbing while the run lasts; a standing wing an author roofed `none` keeps its plan unchanged. V03 §5.6 (2) (c) and V02 §5.7 (2) cite this." Rendering writes §8.6's end in the same round (VAF-R2T-02; R2-05).

issues.claim: §8.6 *The damaged plan* (l.13839–13841) draws "each plan element whose threshold t … its decay level reaches … damaged, every other element as built". That forbids V03 §5.6 (2) (c)'s and V02 §5.7 (2)'s roofless rule: a roof bay of a roofless wing below its threshold is drawn as built (a ceiling) by §8.6 and open by V03, under an exterior V02 draws with no roof. Same defect as VAF-R2T-01, at the drawing's base home.
issues.required_change: §8.6: "… is drawn damaged — and every roof bay over a room of a roofless wing of a `decayed` or `ruined` building, whatever its t (§2.6 step 7's one case without a threshold; V03 §5.6 (2) (c)) — every other element as built."

issues.claim: V02 and V03 scope the roofless rule differently. V02 §5.7 (2), X34 (l.4095) and T-V2-59 (b) (l.3686) apply it to every roofless building — "roof kind `none`, the model's `decayed`, `ruined` and `charred` states" — so its plan's every roof bay is open. V03 §5.6 (2) (c) (l.2697) and its hand-off row to V02 (l.3236, "a wing a decay run leaves roofless") apply it only "in a decay run". V06 §3.23 (4) puts several buildings in no run: those generated `decayed` or `ruined`, those first met so in item 113's replay, and every building before M6-E. Each reads at V11's default age (`defaultAgeYears` 40). A masonry one then lands below the `roofBay` range: ashlar 0.008 × 40 → 1/3, rubble 0.44, brick 0.48, against 0.40–0.66, and before V11's rows ship every `decayed` building sits at 1/3. For such a building, V03 leaves roof bays intact in the plan where V02's exterior shows no roof, and T-V2-59 (b) fails on the fixture V03 draws.
issues.required_change: V03 §5.6 (2) (c): "**(c) Roofless** — while the building is `decayed` or `ruined` (in a decay run, or read at V11's default age with no run in the log, V06 §3.23 (4)) and a wing's roof kind is `none` (§2.6's `RoofSpec`: …), every roof bay over a room of that wing is damaged whatever its threshold (§2.6 step 7) …; once the building's state is `decayed`, each such bay counts as reached for (b) …". V03 §13's V02 row (l.3236): "every roof bay of a roofless wing of a `decayed` or `ruined` building damaged". V03 §3.13's damage-layer row adds the edge "a building generated `decayed` in masonry, and every `decayed` building before M6-E: every roof bay of its roofless wings damaged". T-V3-39 (b) adds that fixture.

issues.claim: Two units disagree on what land a camp may take. V01 §3.16 calls `campLand` "the outskirts' land a camp look may take" (l.2360–2371). It is never wood, marsh, quarry, garden or orchard, and lies within `camp.reachM`. V01 §1b's wiring row (l.283) names `beyondWalls` among its readers, and R2-37 (5) rules "The outskirts' land is V01's `campLand` … §10.2's placement rules rank them". But §10.2 *Crisis looks* (d)'s `beyondWalls` (l.15376–15378) takes "the land faces at least `siegeStandoffM` beyond … (`campLand`'s **and the hinterland's land-use faces** there)": any wood, orchard, quarry, marsh or crop field, at any distance. `approachRoads` (l.15379) defines a second, unbounded set of "verges of each arterial" beside `campLand` (2)'s. (e)'s cap, "`densityCap` of the outskirts' free land" (l.15399), then has no single denominator. So the siege camps stand on land V01 says no camp takes, and the cap's base differs with the reader.
issues.required_change: §10.2 *Crisis looks* (d): "`beyondWalls` — the `campLand` faces (V01 §3.16) lying at least `siegeStandoffM` beyond the outermost standing enceinte's outer strip along its walled arcs; a closure arc with no wall draws none"; "`approachRoads` — `campLand`'s verges of each arterial leaving the settlement (V01 §3.16 (2)), one camp per road; a road with none, and a place no road reaches (…), take the `campLand` nearest its boundary"; (e): "together at most `densityCap` of `campLand`'s free land". (f)'s trenches, earthworks and burned farmsteads, which are no camp, keep their own places. V01 §1b's `campLand` row then reads "`approachRoads`" for "`approachRoads`' fallback" (V01's end, R2-05).

issues.claim: R2-14's class persists outside the six members. V09 §1b's table *The dossier facts this volume shows* (l.409) still reads "a building specified as grand · a dossier record naming a manor, hall or similar (V08's "specified", item 115 (c)) · §4.7 S10b's ceiling, lifted for it". R2-14 retires "hall or similar record" as vaguer than the home: a `town_hall` or `guildhall` record specifies nothing. Both readers of the fact read the home: §4.7 S10b (3), where the ceiling is lifted, and V09 §4.21.5 (2), which shows `info.grand.dossier`. The table row claims the ceiling is lifted, and the why fact "Named in SettlementForge's record" shown, for records S10b does not lift.
issues.required_change: V09 l.409's second cell: "a dossier-bound record of a class in `grandeur.ceiling`'s `settings.grandClasses` (V11 §3.25.4), or a dossier government whose `villageSeat` names the manor house, seigneurial or crown (V11 §3.21.1) — V08 §3.16 (3)'s "specified", item 115 (c)".

The enumeration has two homes, the class R2-13 closes ("a type the base declares is cited by the volumes, never declared twice"). Noted for other seats in round 1 and raised by none.
